name: Black Country (United Kingdom)
description: A field divided vertically black at the hoist and red at the fly, with a white glass-cone shape rising from the base at the centre; a black chain of three links runs across the upper part of the flag.
history: Designed by Gracie Sheppard, an 11-year-old pupil at Redhill School in Stourbridge, and chosen by public vote in a competition run by the Black Country Living Museum after several years of campaigning. Registered with the Flag Institute and unveiled at the museum on 14 July 2012, the tercentenary of the first Newcomen atmospheric engine; the date has since been kept as Black Country Day.

features.symbolism: the region 'black by day and red by night' — Elihu Burritt's 1862 description of its furnaces
the glass cones and furnaces of the region's glass-making and iron industries
